person_note: The controlling narrative is third-person limited with shifting focal characters, not multiple first-person narrators. Numerous long Goodreads passages independently narrate Alex, Lacy, Peter, Josie, Lewis, Jordan, and Patrick externally while accessing their thoughts; authorized opening and interior excerpts show the same pattern, and two whole-book sources explicitly describe every section as third-person limited. The apparent contrary I passages are brief diary-style entries by Josie, courtroom testimony, dialogue, or local direct thought. They do not form an autonomous first-person base strand. Generic you in aphorisms and free-indirect reflections is likewise not sustained second-person narration. No material uncertainty remains about the controlling person.
